VNM.summary: Vietnamese is an Austroasiatic language characterized by monosyllabic roots and 6 distinct vocal tones. It is written in 'Chữ Quốc ngữ', a Latin-based alphabet developed in the 17th century with diacritics denoting tone and vowel quality.

languages.name: Vietnamese
languages.notes: Six-tone language that incorporated extensive Chinese vocabulary (Hán-Việt) over two millennia.

languages.name: Tày & Thai
languages.notes: Spoken by highland ethnic groups with rich agricultural and weaving traditions.

languages.name: Hmong & Khmer Krom
languages.notes: Khmer Krom communities in the Mekong Delta maintain Khmer pagoda schools.

accents.name: Northern (Hanoi)
accents.description: Sharp distinction between all 6 tones, clear glottal stops, 'r'/'d'/'gi' all merge into a smooth /z/ sound.
accents.sample: Xin chào bạn! Hôm nay trời đẹp quá, đi uống cà phê trứng nhé!

accents.name: Central (Huế / Quảng Nam)
accents.description: Heavier, deeper intonation, tone merging (hỏi and ngã merge), distinct regional vocabulary.
accents.sample: Răng mà đẹp rứa? Đi mô đó bạn ơi?

accents.name: Southern (Saigon / Ho Chi Minh City)
accents.region: Ho Chi Minh City & Mekong Delta
accents.description: Relaxed cadence, 'v' pronounced as 'd/y', five tones (hỏi and ngã merge), open friendly rhythm.
accents.sample: Chào anh hai! Đi ăn cơm tấm sườn nướng ngon lắm nè!

phrases.text: Cảm ơn bạn rất nhiều! (Thank you very much)

VNM.funFact: A single syllable in Vietnamese like 'ba' can mean eight completely different things depending solely on tone: 'ba' (three/father), 'bà' (grandmother), 'bá' (earl), 'bả' (bait), 'bã' (residue), and 'bạ' (random)!
VNM.name: Vietnam

languages.name: English (American)
languages.notes: Dominant language of federal government, commerce, and media.

languages.name: Spanish
languages.regions: Southwest, Florida, California, New York, Texas, Puerto Rico
languages.notes: Second largest Spanish-speaking population in the world after Mexico.

languages.name: Chinese (Mandarin & Cantonese)
languages.notes: Established presence since 19th-century gold rush and transcontinental railroad.

languages.name: Tagalog
languages.notes: Fastest growing Asian language community in several Western states.

languages.name: Vietnamese
languages.notes: Official voting materials provided in counties across multiple states.

languages.name: Navajo (Diné Bizaad)
languages.notes: Famous for Code Talkers who transmitted secret military messages in WWII.

languages.name: Hawaiian
languages.notes: Co-official with English in the state of Hawaii under the 1978 State Constitution.

accents.name: General American (GenAm)
accents.description: Standard rhotic American accent, lacking salient regional markers; basis for broadcast media.
accents.sample: Did you catch the water bottle on the table? (flap T: wa-der bah-dl)

accents.name: Southern American English
accents.description: Drawl cadence, monophthongization of /aɪ/ ('ride' sounds like 'rahd'), 'pin-pen' merger, and use of 'y'all'.
accents.sample: Well bless your heart, y'all come on over for some sweet tea!

accents.name: New York City & New Jersey
accents.description: Historically non-rhotic, /ɔ/ vowel raise ('caw-fee', 'tawk'), short-a split ('bad' vs 'bat').
accents.sample: I gotta grab a slice and a regular coffee in Manhattan, forget about it!

accents.name: Boston / New England
accents.description: Famous non-rhotic 'broad A' ('pahk the cah in Hahvahd yahd'), distinct intonation, use of 'wicked'.
accents.sample: That was wicked awesome, grab a tonic from the package store.

accents.name: Midwestern / Northern Cities
accents.description: Northern Cities Vowel Shift: short 'a' raises toward /eə/ ('cat' -> 'kyat'), 'bus' sounds like 'boss'.
accents.sample: Yeah no for sure, don'tcha know we're headed down by the lake.

accents.name: African American Vernacular (AAVE)
accents.description: Rich rule-governed variety with habitual 'be', copula deletion, consonant cluster reduction, and unique prosody.
accents.sample: She be working late every weekday.

accents.name: Appalachian English
accents.description: Preserves archaic Elizabethan English features, intrusive 'r' ('warsh'), prefix a- ('a-hunting').
accents.sample: He was a-talking right smart about them mountain hollows.

accents.name: Hawaiian Pidgin (HCE)
accents.description: Creole combining English with Hawaiian, Portuguese, Cantonese, Tagalog, and Japanese lexical items.
accents.sample: Howzit brah? We go grind some grinds!

phrases.text: Have a great day / Catch you later!

GBR.officialName: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
GBR.summary: The UK is the birthplace of the English language. Remarkably, accent variation changes roughly every 25 miles, from Cockney and RP to Scouse, Geordie, Scottish Gaelic, and Welsh.

languages.name: English (British)
languages.notes: The historic source of worldwide English, characterized by hundreds of regional varieties.

languages.name: Welsh (Cymraeg)
languages.notes: The only de jure official language established by law in any part of the UK; taught in all Welsh schools.

languages.name: Scots
languages.notes: Sister Germanic language to English, celebrated in the poetry of Robert Burns.

languages.name: Scottish Gaelic (Gàidhlig)
languages.notes: Ancient Celtic language with bilingual signage throughout Scotland and BBC Alba broadcasts.

languages.name: Irish (Gaeilge)
languages.notes: Granted official status under the Identity and Language (Northern Ireland) Act 2022.

languages.name: Cornish (Kernowek)
languages.notes: Successfully revitalized from dormancy through dedicated community schooling and cultural efforts.

accents.name: Received Pronunciation (RP / BBC)
accents.description: Non-rhotic prestige accent, trap-bath split, precise enunciation, traditionally associated with Oxford and broadcasting.
accents.sample: One would hardly imagine such delightful weather in autumn.

accents.name: Cockney & Estuary English
accents.description: Glottal stops for /t/, th-fronting ('fink' for think), rhyming slang ('apples and pears' = stairs).
accents.sample: Alright mate, 'ave a butchers at that! Proper sorted.

accents.name: Scouse
accents.description: Throat fricatives (/k/ pronounced with uvular fricative 'ch'), rising intonation at phrase ends, fast tempo.
accents.sample: Alright la, yer sound, lad! Deffo boss that, honest to God.

accents.name: Geordie
accents.description: Rhythmic lilt, Anglo-Saxon archaic vocabulary ('howay', 'bairn', 'scran'), non-rhotic, unique vowels.
accents.sample: Howay the lads! Wey aye man, it's pure class like.

accents.name: Brummie
accents.description: Downward melodic inflection, nasalized quality, distinct vowel shifts ('alright' sounds like 'a-roight').
accents.sample: Alright bab, how's it going? Grab us a cup of tea.

accents.name: Scottish English
accents.description: Rhotic (rolled or tapped 'r'), pure monophthong vowels, distinct vocabulary ('wee', 'dreck', 'ken').
accents.sample: It's a braw bricht moonlicht nicht the nicht, ya ken!

accents.name: Welsh English
accents.description: Melodic sing-song pitch range, prolonged consonants, distinctive tag questions ('isn't it?', 'tidy').
accents.sample: Who's coat is that jacket? That's proper tidy, mun!

phrases.text: How are you doing? / You alright?

GBR.funFact: A person's accent in Great Britain can change noticeably within just 25 miles of travel, reflecting over 1,500 years of isolated linguistic evolution from Anglo-Saxon, Viking, Norman, and Celtic roots.
GBR.name: United Kingdom

languages.notes: North Levantine Arabic spoken along southern border; Zazaki is spoken in eastern mountains.

accents.name: Istanbul Turkish (Standard)
accents.description: Melodic cadence, front vowels, standard for national broadcasting, theatre, and publishing.
accents.sample: Merhaba, nasılsınız? Size bir Türk kahvesi ikram edeyim.

accents.name: Karadeniz (Black Sea)
accents.description: Rapid, percussive tempo, rising melodic pitch, unique maritime folklore and vocabulary.
accents.sample: Uy daa! Ne habersun hemşerim? Hayde gidelum balığa!

accents.name: Aegean / Ege
accents.description: Lengthening of vowels, relaxed sunny cadence, characteristic tag question 'gari'.
accents.sample: N'aber gari? Haydin kordonda çay içip deniz havası alalım.

TUR.funFact: Because Turkish is an agglutinative language, you can build an entire, grammatically complete story in a single 70-letter word: 'Muvaffakiyetsizleştiricileştiriveremeyebileceklerimizdenmişsinizcesine' ('As if you were of those whom we might not be able to easily make a creator of unsuccessful ones')!
TUR.name: Turkey

languages.notes: Historical language of the Lanna Kingdom; gentle and melodic cadence.

languages.name: Southern Thai (Pak Tai)

languages.notes: Known for rapid, truncated speech and up to seven distinct tones.

CHE.summary: Switzerland is famously pluricentric with four national languages, each dominating distinct cantonal regions without a single federal language imposing on another.

languages.name: German (Swiss German)
languages.regions: Northern, Central, and Eastern Cantons (Zurich, Bern, Basel, Lucerne)
languages.notes: Diglossic: Swiss German Alemannic dialects are spoken daily, while Standard Swiss German is used for formal writing.

languages.name: French
languages.regions: Romandy (Geneva, Vaud, Neuchâtel, Jura, Valais, Fribourg)
languages.notes: Uses traditional number words like septante (70) and nonante (90) rather than French soixante-dix.

languages.name: Italian
languages.notes: Influenced by Swiss German administrative loanwords (e.g., natel for mobile phone).

languages.name: Romansh
languages.regions: Canton of Graubünden (Engadin and Surselva valleys)
languages.notes: Ancient Romance language descended from Vulgar Latin spoken by Roman garrisons in Rhaetia.

accents.name: Züritüütsch (Zurich German)
accents.description: Crisp, fast-paced Alemannic dialect with distinct intonation and rounded vowel shifts.
accents.sample: Grüezi mitenand! Wie gaht's eu hüt?

accents.name: Bärndütsch (Bernese German)
accents.description: Characterized by l-vocalization (l becomes u, e.g., 'viu' for 'viel') and melodic elongation.
accents.sample: Äuä! Das isch aber öppis feins gsi!

accents.name: Walliserdütsch (Valais German)
accents.description: Highest-altitude Alemannic dialect retaining archaic Old High German grammatical forms and vowel sounds.
accents.sample: Chrüt und Chabis! D'Alpe sind wunderschön.

accents.name: Suisse Romand French
accents.description: Slightly slower cadence with distinctive lexical items (huitante for 80, poutser for cleaning).
accents.sample: C'est bonard! On se retrouve à la gare à huitante heures.

CHE.funFact: Swiss road signs change language right across cantonal borders, often within a single kilometer, with no border control whatsoever—moving from 'Sortie' in French to 'Ausfahrt' in German!
CHE.name: Switzerland

SWE.summary: Swedish is a North Germanic language renowned for its musical pitch accent (tonal word distinctions). Sweden constitutionally recognizes five national minority languages: Finnish, Meänkieli, Sami, Romani, and Yiddish.

languages.name: Swedish
languages.notes: Tonal pitch accent: 'anden' with accent 1 means 'the duck', while with accent 2 it means 'the spirit'.

languages.name: Sami Languages (Northern, Lule, Southern)
languages.notes: Indigenous reindeer-herding culture with protected language rights in northern municipalities.

languages.name: Finnish & Meänkieli
languages.notes: Historically established minority languages protected under Swedish law.

accents.name: Rikssvenska / Stockholmska
accents.description: Melodic pitch accent, open 'e' and 'ä' vowels, standard for national broadcasting.
accents.sample: Tjena! Ska vi ta en fika på stan?

accents.name: Skånska (Scanian)
accents.description: Diphthongized vowels, uvular 'r' (skorrande r), historically influenced by Danish rule.
accents.sample: Hallå på di! Det var rart att träffa dig.

accents.name: Norrländska
accents.description: Slower tempo, calm intonation, famous ingressive intake of breath ('schuu') meaning 'yes'.
accents.sample: Hejsan! Ska vi ut och åka skidor i fjällen?

SWE.funFact: In Northern Sweden, people routinely say 'yes' simply by inhaling sharply with their lips rounded (a sound like 'schuuup') without ever vocalizing a word—a phenomenon known as an ingressive pulmonary consonant!
SWE.name: Sweden

KOR.summary: Korean is written in Hangul, widely heralded by linguists as the world's most scientifically engineered phonetic alphabet. It features an intricate system of speech levels and honorific verb conjugations.

languages.name: Korean (Hanguk-eo)
languages.notes: Invented by King Sejong the Great in 1443 so commoners could achieve instant literacy.

languages.name: Jeju Language (Jejueo)
languages.notes: Linguistically distinct from mainland Korean; preserves Middle Korean vowels and archaic vocabulary.

accents.name: Seoul Standard (Pyojun-eo)
accents.description: Polite, smooth, soft ending intonations ('-yo', '-ne-yo'), universal in K-dramas and K-pop.
accents.sample: 안녕하세요, 만나서 반가워요! (Annyeonghaseyo, mannaseo bangawoyo!)

accents.name: Gyeongsang-do / Busan Satoori
accents.description: Dynamic tonal pitch accent, fast tempo, strong masculine inflection, blunt and passionate tone.
accents.sample: 밥 묵었나? 맞나! 가시나야, 와 그라는데? (Bap mugeon-na? Matna! Wa geuraneunde?)

accents.name: Jeolla-do Satoori
accents.description: Melodic sing-song cadence, expressive sentence endings ('-heom', '-tang-gae', '-ge-sse-yu').
accents.sample: 오메! 징허게 반갑구마잉! (Ome! Jing-heoge bangap-gumang!)

phrases.text: 안녕히 계세요! (Stay well) / 안녕히 가세요! (Go well)

KOR.funFact: Hangul was scientifically designed so that the shape of each consonant letter literally mirrors the position of the tongue and mouth when producing that sound (e.g. 'ㄱ' mimics the back of the tongue blocking the throat)!
KOR.name: South Korea

ZAF.name: South Africa
ZAF.summary: South Africa boasts 12 constitutional official languages (including South African Sign Language recognized in 2023). Zulu and Xhosa are the most widely spoken native languages, while English serves as the primary language of commerce and government.

languages.name: isiZulu (Zulu)
languages.notes: Features three distinct click consonants (c, q, x) borrowed from Khoisan languages.

languages.name: isiXhosa (Xhosa)
languages.notes: Famous for complex click consonants, spoken by Nelson Mandela and Miriam Makeba.

languages.name: Afrikaans
languages.notes: Daughter language of 17th-century Dutch, with simplified grammar, double negatives, and Malay/Khoi influences.

languages.name: English (South African)
languages.notes: Universal link language in business and politics; incorporates terms like 'braai', 'howzit', 'now-now'.

languages.name: Sepedi (Northern Sotho)
languages.notes: Major language of the northeastern provinces.

languages.name: Setswana (Tswana)
languages.notes: National language of neighboring Botswana and official in South Africa.

accents.name: White South African English
accents.description: Non-rhotic, pin-pen merger, unique vowel shifts ('yes' sounds like 'yis'), use of 'lekker' and 'shame'.
accents.sample: Howzit boet! We're having a lekker braai this weekend, tune me if you're coming.

accents.name: Cape Flats / Coloured Afrikaans
accents.description: Rapid, melodic hybrid of English and Afrikaans (Kaaps), distinctive rhythmic punch and slang.
accents.sample: Aweh my broe! Duidelik, everything is mos reg!

accents.name: Black South African English
accents.description: Syllable-timed, clear open vowels, resonant pitch, incorporating indigenous conversational markers.
accents.sample: Yoh! It's too hot today my friend, sharp sharp!

phrases.text: Sala kahle (Stay well) / Hamba kahle (Go well)

ZAF.funFact: South Africa's national anthem combines verses in five different languages: Xhosa, Zulu, Sesotho, Afrikaans, and English—transitioning seamlessly between different musical keys and languages!

RUS.summary: Russian is the state language across the federation, written in the Cyrillic alphabet. Over 35 co-official languages are recognized in constituent republics, ranging from Tatar and Bashkir to Chechen and Yakut.

languages.name: Russian
languages.notes: Largest native language in Europe; renowned for six grammatical cases and rich literary canon.

languages.name: Tatar
languages.notes: Second most spoken language in Russia; major historical cultural language along the Volga River.

languages.name: Chechen
languages.notes: Ancient Caucasian language with rich ejective consonants and complex noun-class systems.

languages.name: Bashkir & Chuvash
languages.notes: Chuvash is the sole living survivor of the ancient Oghur branch of Turkic.

accents.name: Standard Moscow (Akan'ye)
accents.description: Akan'ye (unstressed 'o' pronounced as 'a'), soft consonants, standard for state television and theatre.
accents.sample: Здравствуйте! Как ваши дела? Всё отлично. (Zdravstvuyte! Kak vashi dela?)

accents.name: Northern Russian (Okan'ye)
accents.description: Okan'ye (clear preservation of unstressed 'o'), softer rhythm, archaic folklore phrasing.
accents.sample: Пойдём ко мне в гости, чай пить будем! (Poydyom ko mne v gosti...)

accents.name: Southern Russian
accents.description: Fricative 'g' (/ɣ/ sound closer to Ukrainian 'h'), softening of final 't', Cossack heritage.
accents.sample: Шо ты кажешь? Давай быстрее! (Sho ty kazhesh?)

RUS.funFact: Despite spanning 11 time zones and over 9,000 kilometers from Saint Petersburg to Vladivostok, spoken Standard Russian displays remarkably little accent variation compared to English or German!
RUS.name: Russia

PRT.summary: European Portuguese is stress-timed, giving it a distinctive rhythmic cadence with reduced unstressed vowels and sibilant 'sh' sounds that foreigners often humorously mistake for a Slavic language. Mirandese is officially recognized in the northeast.

languages.name: Portuguese (European)
languages.notes: Rich in nasal vowels and diphthongs (ão, õe); basis for standard Lusophone grammar.

languages.name: Mirandese (Mirandés)
languages.notes: Officially recognized since 1999; taught in local schools alongside Portuguese.

accents.name: Lisboeta (Lisbon)
accents.description: Palatalized 's' (sounds like 'sh'), closed vowels, smooth metropolitan cadence.
accents.sample: Olá, tudo bem? Vamos beber uma bica e comer um pastel de nata?

accents.name: Tripeiro (Porto / Northern)
accents.description: Distinction of 'b' and 'v' softened, open front vowels, lively and direct temperament.
accents.sample: Ó meu, estás a ver? Aquilo no Porto é que é uma maravilha!

accents.name: Insular (Azores & Madeira)
accents.description: French-like rounded 'u' (/y/) in São Miguel, melodic island cadence.
accents.sample: Bom dia! Como vai essa gente?

PRT.funFact: Because European Portuguese reduces unstressed vowels and uses frequent 'sh' sounds, travelers hearing it for the first time often mistake it for Russian or Polish, even though it is a pure Romance language directly descended from Latin!
PRT.name: Portugal

accents.sample: Cześć! Co tam słychać? Wszystko w porządku!

accents.name: Góralski (Highlander)

POL.name: Poland

PHL.summary: The 1987 Philippine Constitution establishes Filipino (standardized Tagalog) and English as the official languages of communication and instruction, with 19 recognized regional auxiliary languages.

languages.name: Filipino (Tagalog)
languages.regions: Metro Manila, Central and Southern Luzon, Nationwide
languages.notes: Rich in loanwords from Spanish (300+ years of rule) and English.

languages.name: English (Philippine)
languages.notes: One of the world's largest English-speaking populations; basis for thriving global BPO hub.

languages.name: Cebuano (Bisaya)
languages.notes: Second most spoken mother tongue in the Philippines, with vibrant literary tradition.

languages.name: Ilocano & Hiligaynon
languages.notes: Ilocano is the dominant trade language across northern Luzon.

accents.name: Taglish (Manila Urban)
accents.description: Effortless code-switching between Tagalog and English, ubiquitous in media, tech, and everyday conversation.
accents.sample: Tara, let's grab coffee na! Super traffic kasi sa EDSA kanina.

accents.name: Bisaya Accent
accents.description: Crisp vowels, clear rhythmic syllable timing, interchange of 'e' and 'i' or 'o' and 'u', musical inflection.
accents.sample: Maayong adlaw! Mangaon ta ninyo, lami kaayo ang pagkaon!

accents.name: Ilonggo Accent
accents.description: Famous for its extremely gentle, sweet, affectionate, and soothing sing-song melody ('malambing').
accents.sample: Kamusta ka na toto? Palangga guid ka namon.

PER.summary: Peru is constitutionally plurilingual: Spanish is official alongside Quechua, Aymara, and indigenous Amazonian languages where they predominate. Quechua was the imperial language of the Inca civilization.

languages.name: Spanish (Peruvian)
languages.notes: Coastal Limeño Spanish is noted for clear diction and lack of strong regional melody.

languages.name: Quechua (Runa Simi)
languages.notes: The state language of the Inca Empire (Tawantinsuyu); the most spoken indigenous language family in the Americas.

languages.name: Aymara
languages.notes: Unique for its trivalent logic system and conceiving the past as 'in front of us' (since we can see it).

languages.name: Amazonian Languages (Asháninka, Awajún, Shipibo)
languages.notes: Over 40 indigenous languages flourish along the tributaries of the Amazon river.

accents.name: Limeño (Coastal Peruvian)
accents.description: Moderate pacing, clear consonant clusters, polite mannerisms, famous slang (pata, chévere, asu mare).
accents.sample: ¡Asu mare, qué paja! Oye pata, vamos a comer un rico cebichito.

accents.name: Andino (Highland Spanish)
accents.description: Influence of Quechua/Aymara phonology: vowel reduction (e->i, o->u), double possessives ('de mi mamá su casa').
accents.sample: Vente pues, aquicito nomás estamos llegando a la plaza.

accents.name: Amazónico (Selva Spanish)
accents.description: Melodic pitch, sibilant transformation of 'f' and 'j' into a soft aspirated breath, unique vocabulary.
accents.sample: ¡Ay diosito! Vamos al río a pescar paiche con la choche.

PER.funFact: In the Aymara language of Peru and Bolivia, the future is described as being BEHIND you (because it is unknown and unseen), while the past is in FRONT of you (because you can already see and remember it)!
PER.name: Peru

PNG.name: Papua New Guinea
PNG.officialName: Independent State of Papua New Guinea
PNG.diversityLevel: Highest Linguistic Diversity in the World (840+ Languages)
PNG.summary: Papua New Guinea is undisputed as the most linguistically diverse place on planet Earth. With over 840 living indigenous languages spoken across rugged mountain valleys and dense jungles, it contains roughly 12% of all languages on Earth in a single country!

languages.name: Tok Pisin
languages.notes: Highly expressive creole developed on Pacific plantations; official language in parliament.

languages.name: English
languages.notes: Official language of higher schooling and formal law.

languages.name: Hiri Motu
languages.regions: Southern coastal regions around Port Moresby
languages.notes: Historic trading pidgin of the Motu sea expeditions (Hiri voyages).

languages.name: Papuan & Austronesian Indigenous (840+)
languages.notes: Enga is the largest indigenous language with ~230,000 speakers; hundreds have fewer than 1,000 speakers.

accents.name: Highlands Tok Pisin
accents.description: Fast, energetic tempo with deep glottal rhythm and indigenous phonetic substrate.
accents.sample: Gude tru wantok! Yu stap gut o nogat?

accents.name: Coastal & Islands Tok Pisin
accents.description: Melodic, vowel-rich cadence influenced by Austronesian oceanic languages.
accents.sample: Em nau, mipela go long solwara nau tasol.

phrases.text: Yu stap gut? (Are you doing well?)

PNG.funFact: Papua New Guinea is home to over 840 distinct languages! Two villages separated by only a single mountain ridge often speak completely unrelated languages from entirely different language families.

PAK.name: Pakistan
PAK.diversityLevel: Multilingual Federation (Punjabi, Pashto, Sindhi, Balochi, Saraiki)
PAK.summary: Urdu is the national lingua franca and English is the official language. Although Urdu is the primary language of education and national identity, Punjabi, Pashto, Sindhi, and Saraiki are spoken natively by the majority of provincial populations.

languages.name: Urdu
languages.notes: Renowned worldwide for its courtly elegance, ghazal poetry, and Nastaliq calligraphy.

languages.name: Punjabi
languages.notes: Largest native language in Pakistan, celebrated in the Sufi poetry of Bulleh Shah and Waris Shah.

languages.name: Pashto
languages.notes: Language of the Pashtun code of honor (Pashtunwali), with rich tribal oral verse (Tappa).

languages.name: Sindhi
languages.notes: One of South Asia's oldest literary languages, with ancient roots in the Indus Valley.

languages.name: Saraiki & Balochi
languages.notes: Saraiki is famous for sweet Sufi poetry (Kafi); Balochi is an ancient Iranian tongue.

accents.name: Lahori Punjabi-Urdu
accents.description: Rich, hearty, energetic cadence, vibrant food and cultural banter, musical rising tones.
accents.sample: Oye kithe chale o janab? Chalo aao pehle naan-chana khande aan!

accents.name: Karachi Urdu (Muhajir)
accents.description: Refined Lucknow/Delhi classical syntax, crisp diction, rapid cosmopolitan urban slang.
accents.sample: Aray bhai kya baat kar rahay ho! Bilkul first class scene hai.

accents.name: Peshawari / Pashto-Inflected
accents.description: Strong resonant retroflex consonants, polite hospitality terms (Khaistah, Der Meherbani).
accents.sample: Pakhair raghlay! Tea is ready, you are our honored guest.

accents.name: Sindhi-Urdu
accents.description: Gentle implosive consonants (ɓ, ɗ, ʄ, ɠ), melodic pace, deep Sufi reverence (Sain).
accents.sample: Ada khush ahyo? Bhali kare aaya, Allah reham kare!

phrases.text: خدا حافظ ! / اللہ حافظ ! (Khuda hafiz / Allah hafiz)
آپ کا کیا حال ہے؟ (Aap ka kya haal hai?)

PAK.funFact: Urdu is written in the graceful 'Nastaliq' calligraphic script. Because of its complex sloping letters, Urdu newspapers were written completely by hand by master calligraphers (Katibs) all the way into the late 1990s before digital fonts were developed!

NOR.summary: Norway has two official written standards for Norwegian: Bokmål (Book Tongue, 85%) and Nynorsk (New Norwegian, based on rural dialects, 15%). Sami is co-official in northern administrative districts.

languages.name: Norwegian (Bokmål)
languages.notes: Evolved from Dano-Norwegian; dominant standard in media, publishing, and business.

languages.name: Norwegian (Nynorsk)
languages.notes: Created by linguist Ivar Aasen in the 19th century from rural Norwegian dialects.

languages.name: Sami (North, Lule, South)
languages.notes: Co-official with Norwegian under the Sami Act; operates its own Sami Parliament (Sametinget).

accents.name: Østnorsk (Eastern / Oslo)
accents.description: Retroflex consonants, tonal pitch accent 1 and 2, musical rising intonation at phrase ends.
accents.sample: Hei! Koselig å se deg, skal vi ta en kaffe?

accents.name: Vestlandsk (Bergen & Fjords)
accents.description: Uvular 'r' (skarre-r), distinct melody, rich traditional vowel variations.
accents.sample: Eg e'kje fra Norge, eg e' fra Bergen!

phrases.text: Hvordan går det? (How does it go?)

NOR.funFact: Norwegians take immense pride in their local spoken dialects—teachers, television anchors, and even prime ministers speak on air in their own regional dialect rather than switching to a standardized accent!
NOR.name: Norway

NGA.name: Nigeria
NGA.summary: Nigeria is Africa's most linguistically diverse nation with over 500 indigenous languages. English is the official language, while Nigerian Pidgin serves as the beloved nationwide lingua franca alongside major languages Hausa, Yoruba, and Igbo.

languages.name: English (Nigerian)
languages.notes: Official language uniting the federation across ethnic lines.

languages.name: Nigerian Pidgin (Naija)
languages.regions: Lagos, Niger Delta, Urban centers nationwide
languages.notes: Vibrant creole with its own BBC news service (BBC News Pidgin) and global Afrobeats reach.

languages.name: Hausa
languages.notes: Major trans-Sahelian trade language spoken across West Africa.

languages.name: Yoruba
languages.notes: Three-tone language that influenced Afro-Cuban and Brazilian candomblé traditions.

languages.name: Igbo
languages.notes: Tonal language famous for rich proverbs: 'Proverbs are the palm-oil with which words are eaten'.

accents.name: Lagos Street / Nigerian Pidgin
accents.description: High-energy, percussive rhythm, use of 'sha', 'abi', 'wetin', 'wahala', universal in music and street culture.
accents.sample: How you dey my guy? No wahala at all, we dey gidigba!

NZL.summary: New Zealand has three official languages: English (de facto), Te Reo Māori (de jure since 1987), and New Zealand Sign Language (since 2006). Māori words and greetings are woven into everyday Kiwi conversation.

languages.name: English (New Zealand / Kiwi)
languages.notes: Notable for vowel centralization ('fish and chips' sounds like 'fush and chups') and rich Māori loanwords.

languages.name: Māori (Te Reo Māori)
languages.regions: North Island (Waikato, Bay of Plenty, Northland) & Nationwide
languages.notes: Revitalized through Kōhanga Reo (language nests); national anthem sung in Māori before English.

languages.name: Samoan
languages.regions: Auckland (largest Polynesian city in the world)
languages.notes: Third most spoken language in New Zealand.

accents.name: General Kiwi
accents.description: Centralized front vowels (/ɪ/ -> /ə/, 'pin' sounds like 'pun'), rising terminal intonation, high use of 'eh'.
accents.sample: Kia ora mate! Grab some fush and chups, she'll be right, eh?

accents.name: Southland (Murihiku / The Catlins)
accents.description: The only rhotic accent in New Zealand (pronouncing the 'r' in words like 'purple work'), Scottish settler heritage.
accents.sample: Roll on up to the dairy and grab a cheese roll, bairn!

NZL.funFact: New Zealand's national anthem, 'God Defend New Zealand', is by law almost always sung first entirely in Te Reo Māori ('E Ihowā Atua') and then in English at international sporting events like the Rugby World Cup!
NZL.name: New Zealand

NLD.name: Netherlands
NLD.summary: Dutch is the official language of the Netherlands, with West Frisian co-official in the province of Friesland. The Dutch consistently rank as the world's most proficient non-native English speakers.

languages.name: Dutch
languages.notes: Linguistic sibling to English and German; mother tongue of Afrikaans.

languages.name: West Frisian (Frysk)
languages.notes: The closest living genetic relative to the English language on continental Europe.

languages.name: Limburgish
languages.notes: One of the rare tonal languages in Europe, using pitch to distinguish noun plurals.

languages.name: Dutch Low Saxon
languages.notes: Low German dialect continuum stretching into northern Germany.

accents.name: Randstad / Hollandic
accents.description: Guttural 'hard G' (/x/), rolling or uvular 'r', fast-paced direct communication style.
accents.sample: Nou, gezellig toch! Zullen we een bakkie koffie doen?

accents.name: Brabants & Limburgs (Southern Dutch)
accents.description: Warm 'soft G' (/ɣ/), melodic sing-song intonation, famous for the festive greeting 'Houdoe'.
accents.sample: Houdoe en bedankt hè! Kei leuk dat je er bent.

accents.name: Amsterdams
accents.description: Flattened vowels ('a' sounds like 'aa'), rich historic Yiddish-derived slang (mokum, mazzel, gabber).
accents.sample: Hé ouwe gabber! Krijg nou wat, lekker weertje pik!

accents.name: Rotterdams
accents.description: Straightforward, unpretentious, working-class dock cadence, 'natte T' and dry humor.
accents.sample: Niet lullen maar poetsen! Loop naar de pomp joh.

NLD.funFact: Old Frisian and Old English were virtually the same language 1,400 years ago! Even today, the famous rhyme holds true: 'Brea, bûter en griene tsiis is goed Ingelsk en goed Frysk' ('Bread, butter and green cheese is good English and good Friese').

KEN.summary: Under Kenya's 2010 Constitution, Swahili is the national and official language, and English is an official language. Sheng—a dynamic Swahili-English street slang—dominates Nairobi youth culture.

languages.name: Swahili (Kiswahili)
languages.notes: The most widely spoken Bantu language in the world; official language of the African Union.

languages.name: English (Kenyan)
languages.notes: Features British roots blended with local vocabulary ('chapo', 'matatu', 'mwananchi').

languages.name: Kikuyu (Gikuyu)
languages.notes: Largest native mother tongue in Kenya; language of Nobel laureate Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o.

languages.name: Luhya, Luo & Kalenjin
languages.regions: Western Kenya, Lake Victoria basin, Rift Valley
languages.notes: Dholuo and Kalenjin are Nilotic languages, home to world-record marathon runners.

accents.name: Sheng (Nairobi Youth Slang)
accents.description: Rapid hybrid slang blending Swahili, English, Kikuyu, and Luo, with constantly evolving vocabulary.
accents.sample: Niaje wasee! Manze leo kuko poa sana, form ni gani?

accents.name: Coastal Swahili (Pwani / Mombasa)
accents.description: Pure, poetic, classical Kiswahili Sanifu with soft Arabic-influenced cadence and warm greetings.
accents.sample: Hujambo bwana! Karibu sana Mombasa raha, habari ya asubuhi?

phrases.text: Jambo! / Habari gani? (Hello / What's the news?)
Mzuri sana! / Hakuna matata! (Very good / No worries!)

KEN.funFact: The famous phrase 'Hakuna Matata' is real Swahili meaning 'there are no troubles/problems'! Swahili is also one of the rare languages where time is counted from sunrise (7:00 AM is called 'saa moja' - hour one)!
KEN.name: Kenya

JPN.name: Japan
JPN.summary: Japanese utilizes three distinct writing scripts simultaneously (Hiragana, Katakana, and Kanji) along with an intricate honorific system (Keigo). Regional dialects vary dramatically from Tokyo to Osaka and Okinawa.

languages.name: Japanese (Hyōjungo)
languages.notes: Standardized on the Yamanote dialect of Tokyo during the Meiji modernization.

languages.name: Ryukyuan Languages (Okinawan, Miyako, Yaeyama)
languages.notes: Distinct Japonic languages mutually unintelligible with standard Japanese, classified by UNESCO as endangered.

languages.name: Ainu (Aynu itak)
languages.notes: Critically endangered language isolate of Japan's northern indigenous Ainu people.

accents.name: Tokyo Standard (Hyōjungo)
accents.description: Flat pitch accent, standard polite speech, clear articulation heard on NHK broadcasts.
accents.sample: こんにちは、お元気ですか？ (Konnichiwa, o-genki desu ka?)

accents.name: Kansai-ben
accents.description: Warm, rapid, melodic pitch accent, humor-oriented cadence, 'ya nen' instead of 'da', 'ookini' for thank you.
accents.sample: まいど！めっちゃええやん、ほんまにありがとう！ (Maido! Metcha ee yan, honma ni arigatō!)

accents.name: Tohoku-ben (Zūzū-ben)
accents.description: Nasalized vowels, contracted syllables, historically unintelligible to Tokyo speakers; often subtitled on TV.
accents.sample: おばんです！まんま食ったが？ (Obandesu! Manma kuttaga?)

accents.name: Hakata-ben
accents.description: Soft, friendly sentence-ending particles ('-tai', '-bai', '-to'), popular throughout Japan.
accents.sample: なんばしよっと？バリうまかラーメン食べに行こう！ (Nanba shiyotto? Bari umaka rāmen tabe ni ikō!)

phrases.text: ありがとうございます！ (Arigatō gozaimasu!)
さようなら / じゃあまたね！ (Sayōnara / Jā mata ne!)
お元気ですか？ (O-genki desu ka?)

ITA.summary: Standard Italian is based on the 14th-century Florentine dialect of Dante Alighieri. Yet Italy is home to dozens of distinct regional languages (often called 'dialetti') that are linguistically separate Romance languages.

languages.name: Italian (Standard)
languages.notes: Preserves Latin geminate double consonants (notte, fatto) and open musical vowel cadences.

languages.name: Neapolitan (Nnapulitano)
languages.notes: Linguistic ancestor of world-famous songs ('O Sole Mio) with its own distinct vocabulary and grammar.

languages.name: Sicilian (Sicilianu)
languages.notes: Retains Greek, Arabic, and Norman French loanwords from Sicily's rich multicultural history.

languages.name: Venetian (Vèneto)
languages.notes: The historical language of the Venetian Republic; gave the world words like ciao, ghetto, and quarantine.

languages.name: Sardinian (Sardu)
languages.notes: Considered the most phonologically conservative Romance language, closest to classical Latin.

languages.name: German & Ladin
languages.notes: German is co-official in South Tyrol, where ~65% of the local population speaks German as mother tongue.

accents.name: Romano
accents.description: Doubled 'b' and 'g' consonants, truncation of infinitive endings ('annà' for andare), expressive hand gestures.
accents.sample: Aó! Ma che stai a fa? Nnamo a magnà 'na carbonara bona bona!

accents.name: Milano / Lombardo
accents.description: Closed vowels, nasal endings, deletion of final unstressed vowels, fast business tempo.
accents.sample: Uè, figa! Ci becchiamo in centro per un aperitivo veloce, neh?

accents.name: Toscano (Florentine)
accents.description: Famous 'gorgia toscana' where hard 'c' becomes an aspirated 'h' ('la hasa' instead of la casa).
accents.sample: Maremma maiala! Vieni a bere una 'oha-'ohola con la 'annuccia!

accents.name: Napoletano Accent
accents.description: Melodic cadence, shortening of words, central schwa vowel /ə/ on unstressed endings.
accents.sample: Uagliò, sient' a me! Chest' è 'na pizza overamente speciale!

ITA.funFact: The universal greeting 'Ciao' originated from the Venetian phrase 's-ciavo vostro', literally meaning 'I am your humble servant' in the medieval Venetian language!
ITA.name: Italy

IRL.summary: Under Article 8 of the Irish Constitution, the Irish language (Gaeilge) is designated the 'first official language' of Ireland, while English is recognized as the second official language.

languages.name: English (Hiberno-English)
languages.notes: Syntax deeply shaped by the Irish language: 'after' past tense ('I'm after eating my dinner'), lack of simple 'yes'/'no'.

languages.name: Irish (Gaeilge)
languages.regions: Gaeltacht regions (Galway, Kerry, Donegal, Mayo, Cork) & Nationwide schools
languages.notes: Core national language of Ireland, an official language of the European Union, taught in all schools.

accents.name: Dublin Accent
accents.description: Distinction between Northside (flat vowels, glottal stops, 'ye' plural) and Southside (D4 rising inflection).
accents.sample: Story bud? You're grand, come on in and we'll have a cuppa.

accents.name: Cork & Kerry
accents.description: Sing-song musical lilt, upward pitch at end of sentences, rapid rhythm, rich local slang ('boy', 'feck', 'pure').
accents.sample: Like, that was pure daycint boy, absolutely massive so it was!

accents.name: Galway / Connemara
accents.description: Soft, lilting cadence heavily influenced by native Irish-speaking Gaeltacht intonation.
accents.sample: Ah sure look it, God is good and the weather will take up!

phrases.text: Dia duit! (God be with you / Hello)

IRL.funFact: The Irish language has no direct word for 'yes' or 'no'! Instead, speakers answer questions by echoing the verb: for example, if someone asks 'Did you see him?', the answer is literally 'I saw' or 'I did not see'.
IRL.name: Ireland

IRN.name: Iran
IRN.diversityLevel: Multilingual Empire (Persian, Azeri, Kurdish, Gilaki, Arabic, Balochi)
IRN.summary: Persian (Farsi) is the official language of Iran with over 2,500 years of recorded literature from Hafez, Rumi, and Ferdowsi. Iran is ethnically and linguistically pluralistic, with vibrant regional languages spoken by over 40% of its population.

languages.name: Persian (Farsi)
languages.notes: Classical literary language of high poetry, philosophy, and miniature arts;SOV sentence structure.

languages.name: Azerbaijani (Azeri)
languages.notes: Mutually intelligible with Republic of Azerbaijan Turkish; large diaspora in Tehran.

languages.name: Kurdish (Sorani & Kurmanji)
languages.regions: Western Iran (Kordestan, Kermanshah, Ilam, West Azerbaijan)
languages.notes: Rich oral storytelling tradition with epic Dengbêj bards.

languages.name: Gilaki & Mazandarani (Caspian)
languages.notes: Grammatically distinct from Persian; preserves archaic pre-Islamic linguistic structures.

languages.name: Luri & Bakhtiari
languages.notes: Traditional nomadic shepherd confederations with distinct epic musical poetry.

languages.name: Arabic (Khuzestani)
languages.notes: Mesopotamian-influenced Gulf Arabic spoken in Iran's oil-rich coastal province.

languages.name: Balochi
languages.notes: Ancient Iranian language preserving consonantal sounds lost in modern Persian.

accents.name: Tehrani Standard
accents.description: Smooth cadence, transformation of 'ān' into 'ūn' ('Tehrūn', 'nūn' for bread), polite Ta'arof honorifics.
accents.sample: سلام، حالتون چطوره؟ خیلی مخلصیم، بفرمایید در خدمت باشیم!

accents.name: Isfahani
accents.description: Melodic sing-song pitch curve rising at phrase end, lengthening of penultimate vowels, witty mercantile banter.
accents.sample: سلام دادا! شوما خوبی؟ چیطوری؟ دم شما گرم!

accents.name: Shirazi
accents.description: Relaxed, slow, gentle tempo, adding the affectionate suffix '-oo' to nouns (ketaboo, pesaroo).
accents.sample: حالو ولش بکن! بیا بشین یه چای بهارنارنج بخوریم صفا کنیم.

accents.name: Abadani / Southern
accents.description: Warm, energetic, incorporating Arabic loanwords and coastal sea chanties (Ney-Anban rhythm).
accents.sample: کاکا جون ولک! حالت چطوره؟ بریم لب شط سمبوسه بزنیم!

phrases.text: خداحافظ ! / به امید دیدار ! (Khodāhāfez / Be omide didār)

IRN.funFact: Persian culture has an elaborate system of social politeness called 'Ta'arof', where it is customary to politely refuse an offer (such as food or a cab fare) up to three times before accepting it!

IND.summary: India has no single 'national language'. The Indian Constitution recognizes Hindi and English as official languages of the Union government, and enumerates 22 Scheduled Languages representing the Indo-Aryan, Dravidian, Austroasiatic, and Tibeto-Burman families.

languages.name: Hindi

languages.name: English (Indian)
languages.notes: Widely used link language across linguistic borders; rich distinctive idiom and retroflex consonants.

languages.name: Bengali
languages.notes: Nobel laureate Rabindranath Tagore's language, celebrated for its rich literary tradition.

languages.name: Telugu
languages.notes: Famous for vowel endings on every word, earning it the moniker 'Italian of the East'.

languages.name: Marathi
languages.notes: Official language of India's financial capital and the historic Maratha Empire.

languages.name: Tamil
languages.notes: One of the world's longest-surviving classical languages, with Sangam literature over 2,000 years old.

languages.name: Urdu
languages.regions: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Telangana, Jammu & Kashmir

accents.name: South Indian English
accents.description: Crisp retroflex consonants, syllable-timed cadence, distinctive idioms ('do the needful', 'out of station').
accents.sample: Please kindly revert back at the earliest, no problem at all.

accents.sample: Nomoshkar! Let us sit down and discuss literature over chai.

languages.notes: Standardized through Martin Luther's Bible translation; official language in all federal institutions.

languages.name: Low German (Plattdüütsch)
languages.regions: Northern Germany (Hamburg, Bremen, Schleswig-Holstein, Lower Saxony)
languages.notes: Did not undergo the High German consonant shift; closer to Dutch and Old English (water vs Wasser).

languages.name: Upper & Lower Sorbian
languages.notes: Slavic language protected under state constitutions with bilingual school systems and road signs.

languages.name: Danish & Frisian
languages.notes: Protected minority languages with their own political party (SSW) exempt from the 5% threshold.

accents.name: Bairisch (Bavarian)
accents.description: Rolling 'r', distinctive greeting ('Grüß Gott'), rounding of vowels, rich colloquial vocabulary.
accents.sample: Servus! O'zapft is! Des is a pfundige Gaudi!

accents.name: Berlinerisch
accents.description: Direct, dry wit (Berliner Schnauze), 'g' pronounced as 'j' ('jut' for gut), 'wat' instead of 'was'.
accents.sample: Juten Tach! Wat soll der Quatsch denn, wa?

accents.name: Schwäbisch (Swabian)
accents.description: Diminutive ending '-le' (Mädle, Spätzle), 'st' pronounced as 'scht' ('Du bischt'), melodic inflection.
accents.sample: Grüß Gottle! Schaffe, schaffe, Häusle baue!

accents.name: Kölsch (Cologne / Rhineland)
accents.description: Melodic sing-song pitch, 'g' softened to 'j', celebrated in carnival songs and Kölsch brewery culture.
accents.sample: Kölle Alaaf! Et kütt wie et kütt, trink mer noch e Kölsch!

accents.name: Sächsisch (Saxon)
accents.description: Softened unvoiced stops (p->b, t->d, k->g), elongated central vowels, unique eastern rhythm.
accents.sample: Nu gloor, das hammer doch gleich!

phrases.text: Wie geht es Ihnen? / Wie geht's?
phrases.phonetic: vee GAYT es EE-nen / vee GAYTS

DEU.funFact: German compound nouns can theoretically be infinite in length! The Guinness World Record for the longest German word published was 63 letters: Rindfleischetikettierungsüberwachungsaufgabenübertragungsgesetz.

FRA.name: France
FRA.summary: French is the sole official language of the Republic under Article 2 of the French Constitution. However, historic regional languages like Occitan, Breton, Alsatian, Corsican, and Basque persist proudly.

languages.name: French
languages.notes: Regulated by the Académie Française since 1635 to maintain linguistic standards.

languages.name: Occitan (Langue d'Oc)
languages.notes: The historical language of the medieval Troubadours; distinct from French Langue d'Oïl.

languages.name: Alsatian
languages.notes: Alemannic German dialect close to Swiss German, deeply rooted in Alsatian border culture.

languages.name: Breton (Brezhoneg)
languages.notes: The only Celtic language spoken on the European mainland; taught in immersive Diwan schools.

languages.name: Corsican (Corsu)
languages.notes: Closely related to medieval Tuscan and central Italian dialects.

languages.name: Basque (Euskara)
languages.notes: Oldest living language in Europe; has zero demonstrated genetic relationship to any other language family.

accents.name: Parisièn Standard
accents.description: Fast cadence, uvular trill 'r', neutral vowels; standard pronunciation heard on French television and radio.
accents.sample: C'est nickel, on se retrouve au bistrot tout à l'heure.

accents.name: Méridional (Marseille & Provence)
accents.description: Pronunciation of final 'e' caduc, nasal vowels sounded out with an 'ng' finish, lively Mediterranean melody.
accents.sample: Oh bonne mère ! Viens boire un pastis avec nous, peuchère !

accents.name: Ch'ti (Nord-Pas-de-Calais / Picard)
accents.description: Picard dialect influences, 'ch' substituted for 's' sounds ('ti z'aute', 'mi et ti'), warm mining community heritage.
accents.sample: Biloute, comment qu'c'est ? Fait pas biau dehors !

accents.name: Alsatian Accent
accents.description: Germanic tonal cadence, unvoiced stops, distinctive vocabulary borrowings from Alsatian Alemannic.
accents.sample: Hopla ! On mange une bonne tarte flambée ce soir.

FRA.funFact: In 1789 during the French Revolution, only about 12% of France's population actually spoke standard French fluently—the majority spoke regional languages like Occitan, Breton, Flemish, or Basque!

ETH.summary: Ethiopia is one of the only countries in Africa with its own ancient indigenous writing system: the Ge'ez script (Fidel). Ethiopia recognizes 5 working federal languages: Afaan Oromoo, Amharic, Somali, Tigrinya, and Afar.

languages.name: Afaan Oromoo (Oromo)
languages.notes: Largest mother tongue in Ethiopia, written in the official Qubee Latin alphabet since 1991.

languages.name: Amharic (Amarinya)
languages.notes: The historical imperial court language; written in the ancient Ge'ez abugida script.

languages.name: Somali (Af-Soomaali)
languages.notes: Major language of the eastern Horn of Africa, rich in oral pastoral poetry.

languages.name: Tigrinya
languages.notes: Direct sister language to ancient liturgical Ge'ez, also official in Eritrea.

accents.name: Shewa / Addis Ababa Amharic
accents.description: Standard modern spoken Amharic, melodic intonation, glottalized ejective consonants (t', k', p').
accents.sample: ጤና ይስጥልኝ! እንዴት ነዎት? ደህና ነኝ አመሰግናለሁ። (T'ena yist'illign! Endet newot?)

accents.name: Gondar Amharic
accents.description: Deeply traditional cadence, archaic vocabulary, classical royal historical idioms.
accents.sample: እንኳን ደህና መጣችሁ ወደ ታሪካዊቷ ጎንደር!

phrases.text: ሰላም ! / ጤና ይስጥልኝ ! (Peace! / May Health be Given!)
Akkam! / Fayyaa dhaa? (Hello / How is your health?)

ETH.funFact: Ethiopia's Ge'ez script (Fidel) is the only indigenous African writing system still in continuous daily use for millennia! Each character represents a combined consonant and vowel (an abugida).
ETH.name: Ethiopia

EGY.summary: Modern Standard Arabic is the official language of Egypt, while Egyptian Arabic (Masri) is the most widely understood spoken Arabic dialect in the entire world, popularized across the Middle East through Cairo's cinema and music industries.

languages.name: Arabic (Egyptian / Masri)
languages.notes: Pronounces classical 'jim' (ج) as a hard 'g' /g/, and glottalizes 'qaf' (ق) into a hamza 'ʔ'.

languages.name: Modern Standard Arabic (Fus'ha)
languages.notes: Official language of the state and Quranic liturgical study.

languages.name: Sa'idi Arabic
languages.notes: Traditional dialect retaining conservative phonetic and lexical traits.

languages.name: Nubian & Siwi Berber
languages.notes: Siwi is Egypt's only indigenous Berber language, spoken in the western desert oasis of Siwa.

accents.name: Cairene (Cairo Masri)
accents.description: Soft, humorous, rapid, hard 'g' for jim, famous across the Arab world as the Hollywood of Arabic media.
accents.sample: إزيك يا باشا؟ عامل إيه؟ منور والله يا غالي!

accents.name: Alexandrian (Iskandarani)
accents.description: Sing-song cadence, distinctive local terms ('aywah', 'kebdah', 'falafel' called 'ta'meya').
accents.sample: يا جدع، إيه الحلاوة دي؟ يلا نتمشى على الكورنيش ناكل أيس كريم.

accents.name: Sa'idi (Upper Egypt)
accents.description: Pronunciation of 'qaf' as a hard 'g', conservative grammar, proud tribal poetic heritage.
accents.sample: يا مرحب بيك يا ولد عمي! نورت الصعيد كله.

phrases.text: أهلاً وسهلاً ! / صباح الخير ! (Welcome / Good morning)
شكراً جزيلاً يا فندم ! (Thank you very much)
إزيك؟ عامل إيه؟ (How are you doing?)
مفيش مشكلة / معلش (No problem / Never mind)

EGY.funFact: Because Egyptian film, television, and pop music dominated the 20th-century Arab world, almost every Arabic speaker from Morocco to Iraq can instantly understand and speak the Cairo accent!
EGY.name: Egypt

COL.summary: Colombian Spanish—especially the highland Bogotano dialect—is internationally celebrated for its clear enunciation and preservation of classical grammar. The country also recognizes 65 indigenous languages and two creoles.

languages.name: Spanish
languages.notes: Standard Bogotano Spanish is widely regarded as one of the clearest and most melodic forms of Spanish.

languages.name: Wayuu (Wayuunaiki)
languages.notes: The most widely spoken indigenous language in Colombia, spoken by the nomadic Wayuu people.

languages.name: Palenquero Creole
languages.notes: The only Spanish-based creole language in the Americas, declared Intangible Cultural Heritage by UNESCO.

languages.name: San Andrés Creole (Kriol)
languages.regions: Archipelago of San Andrés, Providencia and Santa Catalina
languages.notes: English-derived creole spoken by the indigenous Raizal islanders.

accents.name: Rolo / Bogotano
accents.description: Careful, clear articulation, preservation of 's', formal use of 'usted' even among close family members.
accents.sample: ¿Qué hubo, mi hermano? ¿Quiere tomarse un tintico calientico?

accents.name: Paisa
accents.description: Warm, sing-song intonation, frequent voseo ('vos sabés'), diminutives ('chiquitico'), use of 'parce' / 'parcero'.
accents.sample: ¡Eh ave maría pues! ¿Bien o no parce? ¡Hágale con ganas!

accents.name: Costeño
accents.description: Fast Caribbean tempo, aspiration and omission of final 's', lively cadence influenced by salsa and vallenato.
accents.sample: ¡Ajá, cuadro! ¿Cómo e' la vaina? Vamos pa' la playa.

accents.name: Caleño
accents.description: Characteristic melodic drag, voseo, nasal transitions, world capital of salsa speech.
accents.sample: ¿Mirá vé, vamos a rumbear a Juanchito esta noche?

COL.funFact: San Basilio de Palenque in northern Colombia was the first free African town in the Americas (founded in 1603 by runaway enslaved people) and developed Palenquero, the only Spanish-Bantu creole language on the planet!

CHN.summary: Standard Mandarin (Putonghua) is the national language, based on Beijing phonology. The Chinese linguistic family comprises hundreds of spoken varieties that are as mutually unintelligible as French is to Romanian, yet unified by a common written logographic script.

languages.name: Mandarin (Putonghua)
languages.nativeName: 普通话 / 现代标准汉语
languages.notes: Based on the northern Beijing dialect with 4 distinct tones.

languages.name: Cantonese (Yue)
languages.notes: Preserves ancient Middle Chinese final consonants (-p, -t, -k, -m) with 6 to 9 distinct tones.

languages.name: Wu (Shanghainese)
languages.notes: Distinguished by voiced consonants (b, d, g, z, v) and complex tone sandhi systems.

languages.name: Min Nan (Hokkien / Taiwanese)
languages.notes: Retains the most archaic phonological features, tracing back directly to Old Chinese.

languages.name: Tibetan
languages.notes: Sacred language of Tibetan Buddhism with classical literature dating to the 7th century.

languages.name: Uyghur
languages.notes: Karluk Turkic language closely related to Uzbek, written in a modified Perso-Arabic script.

accents.name: Beijing Dialect (Erhua)
accents.description: Heavy retroflex rhoticity ('erhua' 儿化), rapid speech tempo, crisp alveolar affricates.
accents.sample: 您好！今天这天儿真倍儿棒！ (Nín hǎo! Jīntiān zhè tiānr zhēn bèir bàng!)

accents.name: Sichuanese (Chuan-Yu)
accents.description: Warm, sing-song tonal pattern, soft retroflexes, rich culinary and comedic idiom.
accents.sample: 巴适得板！要得嘛，我们去吃火锅！ (Bāshì de bǎn! Yàode ma, wǒmen qù chī huǒguō!)

accents.name: Southern Mandarin (Jiangnan / Taiwan)
accents.description: Soft consonants, loss of retroflex distinction (zh->z, ch->c, sh->s), expressive end-particles (啦, 嘛, 咧).
accents.sample: 你好啊，真的一点都不麻烦啦！ (Nǐ hǎo a, zhēnde yīdiǎn dōu bù máfan la!)

phrases.text: 你好吗？ / 最近怎么样？ (Nǐ hǎo ma?)

CHN.funFact: While spoken Chinese varieties like Cantonese, Mandarin, and Shanghainese are as phonetically different as Spanish is from German, their speakers can effortlessly read the exact same written text thanks to the shared logographic Chinese character system!

CHL.summary: Chilean Spanish is widely considered the fastest and most distinctive variety in Latin America, characterized by rapid tempo, dropping of final consonants, specialized conjugations ('cachái', 'estái'), and indigenous Mapuche loanwords.

languages.name: Spanish (Chilean)
languages.notes: Unique verbal voseo (tú cachái, tú soi), rapid intonation, and extensive Mapudungun substrate.

languages.name: Mapudungun (Mapuche)
languages.notes: Language of the Mapuche people who famously resisted Incan and Spanish conquest for centuries.

languages.name: Rapa Nui
languages.notes: Eastern Polynesian language spoken on Easter Island; closely related to Hawaiian and Tahitian.

accents.name: Chileno Central (Santiago)
accents.description: Extremely fast tempo, dropping of /s/ and /d/ ('cansao', 'voh sabí'), ubiquitous particles 'po' and 'cachái'.
accents.sample: ¡Wena po, weón! ¿Cachái lo que pasó ayer? ¡La dura!

accents.name: Chilote
accents.description: Archaic Andalusian and Galician vocabulary preserved by island geography, melodic rising pitch.
accents.sample: Ando con frío en las pataguas, vamos pa'l fogón.

CHL.funFact: Chilean Spanish uses the particle 'po' (a contraction of 'pues') at the end of almost every statement ('sí po', 'ya po', 'no po'), giving Chilean conversations an unmistakable, affectionate rhythmic bounce!
CHL.name: Chile

CAN.summary: Canada is constitutionally bilingual at the federal level, with English and French enjoying equal status in parliament, courts, and federal institutions. Quebec is solely French-official.

languages.name: English (Canadian)
languages.notes: Features Canadian Raising of vowels before voiceless consonants and distinctive Canadianisms ('eh').

languages.name: French (Canadian / Québécois)
languages.notes: Retains 17th-century classical French pronunciations, nasal vowels, and anglicism legislation (Bill 101).

languages.name: Indigenous Languages (Cree, Inuktitut, Ojibwe)
languages.notes: Inuktitut and Inuinnaqtun are official languages in Nunavut alongside English and French.

languages.name: Punjabi
languages.notes: Third most spoken language in Canada after English and French.

accents.name: Standard Canadian English
accents.description: Canadian Raising ('about' -> /əˈbʌʊt/), cot-caught merger, rhotic, polite rising intonation ending in 'eh?'.
accents.sample: Pass me the toque before we head out to the rink, eh?

accents.name: Québécois French
accents.description: Affrication of /t/ and /d/ before high front vowels ('tu' sounds like 'tsu', 'dire' like 'dzir'), dipthongized vowels.
accents.sample: C'est tiguidou! On va jaser un peu.

accents.name: Newfoundland English (Newfie)
accents.description: One of the most distinct dialects in the English-speaking world, influenced by Irish and West Country British accents.
accents.sample: Whaddya at, b'y? Stay where you're to till I comes where you're at.

accents.name: Acadian French (Chiac)
accents.description: Maritime French variety blending 17th-century archaic French vocabulary with contemporary English syntax.
accents.sample: J'ai backé mon char dans la driveway.

phrases.text: How's it going, eh? / Comment ça va?
phrases.phonetic: howz it goh-ing, eh? / koh-mahn sah VAH?

CAN.funFact: New Brunswick is the only constitutionally official bilingual province in Canada where government services must be provided in both English and French simultaneously.

AUT.summary: German is the official language of Austria. Austrian German is a distinct standard variety with unique legal and culinary vocabulary recognized by the European Union, complemented by rich Austro-Bavarian and Alemannic dialects.

languages.name: German (Austrian Standard)
languages.notes: Official in all state matters with distinct Austrian protocol terms (Matura, Jänner, Paradeiser).

languages.name: Bavarian / Austro-Bavarian
languages.regions: Vienna, Lower Austria, Salzburg, Tyrol, Styria, Carinthia
languages.notes: Daily spoken vernacular across most Austrian federal states.

languages.name: Burgenland Croatian, Hungarian & Slovenian
languages.notes: Constitutionally protected historical minority languages with bilingual schools.

accents.name: Wienerisch (Viennese)
accents.description: Melodic, relaxed cadence, famous Viennese 'Grant' (dry complaining humor) and soft diphthongs.
accents.sample: Servas! Gehn ma auf a Melange ins Kaffeehaus, bittscheen!

accents.name: Tyrolean (Tirolerisch)
accents.description: Strong aspirated 'k' (kch sound), guttural alpine rhythm, proud mountain idiom.
accents.sample: Griaß di! Des isch a mords Gaudi auf der Alm!

AUT.funFact: When Austria joined the European Union in 1995, Protocol No. 10 of the Accession Treaty explicitly guaranteed that 23 Austrian German food and agricultural words (like 'Erdapfel' for potato and 'Marille' for apricot) have official legal status in EU law!

AUS.name: Australia
AUS.summary: Australian English is famous for its distinctive vowel shifts, extensive hypocoristics (abbreviating words with -o or -ie, like 'arvo' and 'barbie'), and high rising terminal intonation.

languages.name: English (Australian)
languages.notes: Evolved from Cockney and Irish English spoken by early penal colony settlers.

languages.name: Aboriginal & Torres Strait Languages
languages.notes: Over 250 distinct languages existed prior to European arrival; vigorous revival movements are underway.

languages.name: Mandarin Chinese
languages.notes: The most widely spoken language at home in Australia after English.

languages.name: Arabic & Vietnamese
languages.notes: Prominent communities with extensive community schools and bilingual media.

accents.name: General Australian
accents.description: The standard spoken by the majority: non-rhotic, /aɪ/ vowel widened, high rising intonation question pitch.
accents.sample: G'day mate, how's it going? Grab an iced coffee from the servo.

accents.name: Broad Australian
accents.description: Stronger vowel elongation, slower nasal drawl, epitomized by Steve Irwin and Paul Hogan.
accents.sample: Fair dinkum, mate! That croc is an absolute beauty, no worries at all!

accents.name: Cultivated Australian
accents.description: Historically aligned closely with British Received Pronunciation, less common in contemporary speech.
accents.sample: One would certainly appreciate the theatrical production this evening.

accents.name: Aboriginal English
accents.description: Distinctive rhythm, grammatical features influenced by indigenous mother tongues, specific vocabulary ('mob', 'deadly').
accents.sample: That's deadly, sis! Whole mob is coming down for the corroboree.

AUS.funFact: Australians are the world's champions of linguistic abbreviations (hypocoristics): breakfast becomes 'brekkie', afternoon becomes 'arvo', barbecue becomes 'barbie', and avocado becomes 'avo'!

Australia.name: Australia

ARG.summary: Argentine Spanish is world-famous for 'yeísmo rehilado' (pronouncing 'll' and 'y' as 'sh' or 'zh') and 'voseo' (using 'vos' instead of 'tú'). Heavily shaped by 19th/20th-century Italian immigration.

languages.name: Spanish (Rioplatense)
languages.notes: Uses Lunfardo slang, Italian intonation curves, and universal voseo ('vos tenés', 'vos sos').

languages.name: Guarani
languages.notes: Co-official language in the province of Corrientes alongside Spanish since 2004.

languages.name: Quechua
languages.notes: Santiagueño Quechua has been spoken in northern Argentina for hundreds of years.

languages.name: Welsh (Cymraeg)
languages.notes: Spoken by descendants of Welsh settlers who established Y Wladfa in Patagonia in 1865.

accents.name: Porteño (Buenos Aires)
accents.description: Dramatic Neapolitan Italian intonation, 'll'/'y' pronounced as 'sh' ('sho me shamo'), extensive Lunfardo.
accents.sample: ¿Che, boludo, viste la lluvia? ¡Qué quilombo el subte!

accents.name: Cordobés
accents.description: Prolongation of pre-tonic vowels ('Cooordoba'), cheerful singsong cadence, famous for humor.
accents.sample: ¿Qué hacé' culeao? ¡Vamos a tomar un fernet con coca!

accents.name: Cuyano
accents.description: Chilean-influenced rhythm, preservation of older Spanish vowel nuances, distinctive andean vocabulary.
accents.sample: Vea cumpa, vamos a catar un buen Malbec.

ARG.funFact: Patagonia in southern Argentina has the only thriving Welsh-speaking community outside Wales, with bilingual road signs, tea rooms, and an annual Eisteddfod festival!
ARG.name: Argentina
